评审档位：standard（用户显式覆盖；风险评分 6；命中信号：变更 60 行 (+1)、涉及 4 个文件 (+1)、新增或修改网络/数据库/支付外部调用 (+3)、修改测试断言或启用状态 (+1)）

1. [consensus] [Important] compare() compares Dnum tuples lexicographically, not numerically
   证据：src/operations.ts:79 `  return num1_ > num2_ ? 1 : num1_ < num2_ ? -1 : 0;`
   num1_/num2_ are Dnum tuples, so `>`/`<` stringify them: compare(9, 10) returns 1 and compare(0.1, 0.02) returns -1 (wrong). Compare the bigint coefficients `num1_[0]`/`num2_[0]`, as equal() does.
   发现者：correctness, security, design, test-integrity；voter：valid — voter1: Dnum tuples stringify; compare(9,10) returns 1. Comparing coefficients fixes it.

2. [consensus] [Important] compare() tests cannot detect the tuple-coercion ordering bug
   证据：test/all.test.ts:289 `    expect(compare(1n, -1n)).toBe(1);`
   Only single-digit ±1 operands are tested; sort inputs normalize to equal-length coefficients (10000n–80000n), so lexicographic ordering still passes. Add compare(9, 10) or compare(0.1, 0.02).
   发现者：correctness, design；voter：valid — voter1: Only 1n/-1n cases; sort values accidentally order correctly lexicographically.

3. [solo] [Important] Sort test only uses equal-width coefficients, hiding broken compare()
   证据：test/all.test.ts:300 `      ].sort(compare),`
   All sorted inputs normalize to 5-digit coefficients (10000…80000,4), so string-coerced comparison accidentally sorts correctly. No cross-magnitude (9 vs 10) or same-sign negative case exposes the bug.
   发现者：test-integrity；voter：valid — voter1: Sort pairs are equal-width; lexicographic compare still yields expected order.
